name: maybe_Ui_Part_RemapChildPointer
signature: void maybe_Ui_Part_RemapChildPointer(UiPart* self, u32* slot, UiPartOwner* owner)
summary: Remaps the pointer stored in slot[1] through the owner's virtual +0x24, with owner+0x60C temporarily pointing at that slot so the owner can see which field is being fixed up; the result is written back and the marker cleared. Nothing is moved, so the old 'MoveChildSlot' wording described the wrong operation.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00229550: `add r4,r1,#4; str r4,[r2,#0x60c]; ldr r1,[r1,#4]; adds ip,r0,#0x98; ldr r6,[r0,#0x24]; blx r6; str r1,[r4]; str r0,[r5,#0x60c]` - a pointer value is passed through the owner's vtable slot +0x24 and stored back; no slot is moved. The owner marker at +0x60C is a fixup context, not a destination.

name: maybe_Ui_Selection_AdvanceAndClamp
summary: Advances the index at self+0xB0 by one and clamps it twice: first to [0, wcslen(&self+0x184)] (the 0-terminated u16 entry array), then to 0x33 (51). The decompiled C is wrong - Ghidra decoded the wcslen call as a noreturn tail call - so the old 'TriggerCallback' name described a call that does not exist.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0022AB18: `sub r4,r0,#0x4c; ldr r0,[r0,#0xb0]; add r0,r0,#1; str r0,[r4,#0xfc]; add r0,r4,#0x1d0; blx 0x100b74` (wcslen) followed by two min/max clamp sequences ending `str r1,[r4,#0xfc]` with the bound 0x33. The field layout (+0xFC index, 0-terminated u16 array at +0x1D0, capacity 0x34) matches the named Ui_SkillPanel_RemoveEntry (0x0022A9F8), which reads the same index and array.

name: maybe_Actor_EndStateChainEx_Cont
summary: Interior label, not a function: the disassembly at 0x00233DBC starts with `bl 0x1E158C` and has no prologue, so it is a continuation of maybe_Actor_EndStateChainEx (0x00233BEC, which does push {r4-r8,lr}). The body is halt_baddata, so nothing more can be said.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00233DBC begins with `bl #0x1e158c` (Field_ActorJumpTask_Ctor) and no push, while 0x00233BEC begins with `push {r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,lr}`; the xref 'caller' 0x00233BEC is therefore the enclosing function, not a caller. The old name described a teardown that the fragment cannot be shown to perform.

name: maybe_Battle_UnitMatchesHandle
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_UnitMatchesHandle(BattleUnit* self, u32 handle, u8* other)
summary: Handle/ID match test: masks the argument and self+0x39C with the same constant, compares both the masked index and the shifted generation, then compares the byte at self+0x3A0 with a byte taken from the third argument. The old 'ApplyPartMaskToModel' name came from the caller and does not fit a comparison.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0023B6F4: `push {r4-r8,sb,sl,fp,lr}; sub sp,sp,#0x8c; ldr r8,[pc,#0x34c]; ldrb fp,[sl,#0x95]; and r0,r1,r8,asr #10; ldr r1,[r4,#0x39c]` then at 0x0023B734 `and fp,r1,r8,asr #10; cmp r0,fp; lsreq r0,r5,#0xb; cmpeq r0,r1,lsr #11; moveq r0,#1; movne r0,#0` and `ldrb r0,[r4,#0x3a0]; ldrb fp,[r2]; cmp r0,fp`. The 64-byte size in the index is a truncation: the function continues at 0x0023B734.

name: maybe_Battle_UnitMatchesHandle_Cont
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_UnitMatchesHandle_Cont(BattleUnit* self, u32 handle, u8* other)
summary: Continuation of 0x0023B6F4 (no prologue at this address): the masked handle comparison and the +0x3A0 byte comparison, followed by the rest of the match test. It is a separate symbol only because Ghidra split the function here.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0023B734 starts with `and fp,r1,r8,asr #10` - no push - and 0x0023B6F4+0x40 is exactly this address, so it is the second half of the function that starts at 0x0023B6F4. The old 'CompareTargetHandles' guess was close in spirit but named a separate function that does not exist.

name: maybe_Ui_Toggle_UpdateAllNodes
summary: Per-frame node update: takes the transform context from self->f_50's virtual +0xC, runs the node updater 0x00245C80 over the child array at +0x24 (count +0x1C) and over the twelve fixed sub-nodes at +0x30..+0x9C, then walks the auxiliary list at +0x48. The 'update all nodes' part is verified; the Ui_Toggle class is not.
evidence: The body is unchanged and still shows the transform context plus the twelve fixed sub-node updates, so the operation is confirmed. What is missing is the class: the only named callee, 0x00245BC0 'Ui_Toggle_FreeHandle', has 35 callers (Gfx_Node_Attach, Script_SqValueList_Ctor, Sq_VmCreateClass, ...), so it is a generic release helper and does not prove a toggle widget.

name: Ui_Window_SetRecordValue
signature: void Ui_Window_SetRecordValue(UiWindow* self, u32 owner, UiRecord* record)
summary: Stores a two-word record into a window node and links the node into the owner's list at +0x4A8: copies record+8/+0xC into self+0x30/+0x34, points self+0x2C back at self, and does nothing for an all-zero record.
evidence: The caller is now named: Ui_TsuyosaWindow_ApplyModeRecord (0x002A007C) applies a main-menu mode record to the strength window and calls this to store the record's two words in the window node. The list splice helper 0x001235A4 is still unnamed, but the store-and-link shape is the same in the twin 0x002614C8.

name: maybe_Ui_LoadScreen_CloseAndFlush
summary: Unlinks the event payload at ev+0xA8 from the widget's list (0x00123594) and then starts the state machine at self+0x25A0 with argument 1 (0x0029126C). Both helpers are still unnamed, so 'close and flush' remains a description of the call shape.
evidence: No new named neighbour: 0x00123594 and 0x0029126C are both still missing from the readable tree. The only new fact is that 0x0029126C is the same state-machine start that the named Ui_TsuyosaWindow_ApplyModeRecord uses on its +0x138 pane, which supports 'start/flush' but not the 'close' half.

name: maybe_Ui_LoadScreen_RequestTransition
summary: Interior label of the state handler at 0x0025BB08 (no prologue here): after the readiness checks it requests transition 0x3C on the state machine at self+0x11C when the alternate mode is reported, otherwise 0x1D, and returns 1. The old 'State3C' name read the fragment as a whole state handler.
evidence: Disassembly: 0x0025BB08 is the real entry (`push {r4,r5,r6,lr}`), and 0x0025BB2C starts with `bl #0x249074` mid-body. The fragment itself is `ldr r0,[r4,#0x11c]!; mov r1,#0x3c; ldr r2,[r0,#0x14]; blx r2` versus `mov r1,#0x1d` in the other branch, i.e. a transition request, not a state handler. The class prefix is supported by the named neighbour Ui_LoadScreen_State37Or39 (0x0025B768), which is the same load-screen state-handler family.

name: maybe_Ui_LoadScreen_ApplyModeToPane
summary: Small forwarder: calls 0x006722D8 on self+0x718, reads the signed mode byte at self+0x724 and tail-calls 0x00248870(self+0x810, mode). Both callees are still unnamed, so only the call shape is known.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0025BBC8: `push {r4,lr}; add r0,r0,#0x400; add r0,r0,#0x318; bl #0x6722d8; ldr r0,[pc,#0xc]` (=0x724) `; ldrsb r1,[r0,r4]; add r0,r4,#0x810; pop {r4,lr}; b #0x248870`. The literal 0x724 is the field offset, so the tail call passes *(s8*)(self+0x724). Neither the batch name (Save_LoadTask_StartSlotFromTable) nor the index name (SetPaneAnimation) is supported by this; the function forwards a mode byte to the widget at +0x810. The Ui_LoadScreen prefix is supported by the named neighbour Ui_LoadScreen_State37Or39 (0x0025B768) in the same family.

name: Ui_CompositeWindow_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the large composite window: calls the destructor body at 0x002609DC (maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_Dtor, which resets the vtable and destroys about forty embedded sub-objects) and then operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: Disassembly 0x002609CC: `push {r4,lr}; bl #0x2609dc; pop {r4,lr}; b #0x10f6cc` - the canonical deleting-destructor shape. The destructor body 0x002609DC is now named maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_Dtor (its callees are all destructors: Ui_Object_DtorBase, Ui_MessagePage_Dtor, Ui_LayoutRef_Release, Pack_ReleaseHandle), so the 'training window' attribution of the first pass is wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_TrainingWindow_StoreRowRecord
signature: void maybe_Ui_TrainingWindow_StoreRowRecord(UiTrainingWindow* self, u32 owner, UiRecord* rec)
summary: Twin of 0x0025841C with different offsets: stores rec[0]/rec[1] into self+0xDD8/+0xDDC, points self+0xDD4 back at self and splices the node into owner+0x80; no-op for an all-zero record. The class is still inferred from the training-window neighbourhood.
evidence: No named caller and no named callee beyond the generic list splice 0x001235A4 (the xref's 'Snd_DetachChannel' is a misnamed list unlink). The twin 0x0025841C is now confirmed by its named caller, which supports the store-and-link reading but not the training-window class.

name: maybe_Ui_TrainingWindow_SetScriptValue
signature: void maybe_Ui_TrainingWindow_SetScriptValue(UiTrainingWindow* self, u32 value, u8 flag, u32 slot)
summary: Writes value at self+slot, stores flag at self+0xFE0, then measures the wide string returned by 0x00636E54(self+0x11E8, 0x10) with wcslen. The tail is a wcslen call whose result Ghidra dropped, not a noreturn report, so the function is a plain setter plus a length probe.
evidence: 0x00100B74 is wcslen (FACTS.md: Thumb blx to CRT helpers) and the disassembly shows the normal return path after it; the 'Subroutine does not return' warning in the readable C is the known Ghidra trap, so the first pass's 'error/diagnostic path' reading is wrong. The class is still only the training-window neighbourhood.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ScriptCmdJ_ContA
summary: Interior label of the window script-command handler at 0x00263A70 (maybe_Ui_Window_ScriptCommandHandlerJ): the fragment is the first `bl 0x0029126C(sub, 0)` stop call of the handler. It is not a separate close routine.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00263AE8 is `bl #0x29126c` with no prologue, and 0x00263A70 is the real entry (`push {r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,lr}`); the dispatch table at 0x0072B5D8 holds only 0x00263A70, so this address is not a handler of its own. The old 'ClosePartA' name assumed a close routine that the parent's name (script-command handler J) does not support.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ScriptCmdJ_ContB
summary: Interior label of 0x00263A70: the second `bl 0x0029126C(sub, 0)` stop call of the window script-command handler.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00263AF4 is `bl #0x29126c` with no prologue; 0x00263A70 is the enclosing function and the only entry in the 0x0072B5D8 dispatch table. The decompiled body is a misplaced copy routine and cannot be read as code of this address.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ScriptCmdJ_ContC
summary: Interior label of 0x00263A70: the third `bl 0x0029126C(sub, 0)` stop call of the window script-command handler.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00263B24 is `bl #0x29126c` with no prologue; the enclosing function is 0x00263A70. The decompiled body (`(*arg2)(); return 1;`) is unrelated code.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ScriptCmdJ_ContD

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ScriptCmdJ_ContE
summary: Interior label of 0x00263A70: the fifth `bl 0x0029126C(sub, 0)` stop call and the following animation-id dispatch. The decompiled body is unrelated float/scene code.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_BuildDetailWidget_Cont
summary: Interior label of 0x00263BEC (maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_BuildDetailWidget): the fragment runs the state-reset helper 0x0029126C and then dispatches on key-mask bits. Ghidra marked the address Thumb although it is ARM, so the body is halt_baddata.

name: maybe_Ui_TrainingWindow_HandleSlotInput
summary: Per-frame input for one member row: dispatches on the flag word at +0x10A0 - bit 0 runs the row action at +0x820 with the bytes +0x10A2..+0x10A4 and marks the child at +0x11E4 dirty with a sound id, bit 2 requests transition 3, the 0x142 mask resolves the sound id and requests 7/9/10 - then sets +0x11DA.
evidence: The body is readable and unchanged, and the dispatch is verified; what is still missing is the class. The two named callees (0x006508D4, 0x0066699C) are called through different addresses (0x00650954, 0x0066699C) and neither pins the training window, so the class stays inferred from the +0x10A0/+0x11E4 layout.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ScriptTableData
summary: Not code: two data words (0x0072B570 and 0x0072B6A0) sitting in .text between the window constructor and the deleting destructor. Both point into the window action-script dispatch table that starts at 0x0072B570, so this is table data, not an alignment gap.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00264CD8: `rsbseq fp,r2,r0,ror r5` / `rsbseq fp,r2,r0,lsr #13` - the words are 0x0072B570 and 0x0072B6A0. 0x0072B570 is the base of the window action-script dispatch table (0x00263A70 is one of its entries at 0x0072B5D8) and 0x0072B6A0 is an entry inside the same 8-byte {handler,0} table (it holds 0x002638D8), so the pair is table data, not a begin/end range. The old 'AlignGap' name described padding.

name: Ui_CompositeWindow_DtorDeleteB
summary: Deleting destructor of the second composite window: calls the destructor body at 0x00264CF0 (maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_DtorB, which resets the vtable and destroys the embedded message pages, layout refs and child arrays) and then operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00264CE0: `push {r4,lr}; bl #0x264cf0; pop {r4,lr}; b #0x10f6cc`. 0x00264CF0 is the same function as 0x00264CF4 (it loads the vtable into r1 and 0x00264CF4 is the `push` of the body), and 0x00264CF4 is named maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_DtorB - so the class is the composite window, not a 'window part'.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_EmbeddedVtableBlock
summary: Not code: 0x11C bytes of pointers in .text right after the composite-window destructor (0x0072B570, 0x003E04BC, 0x0076EB8C, 0x00782E5C, ...). The 14 'callers' in the xref are noise from the data being read as instructions.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00264FC8 decodes to `rsbseq`/`ldrhteq` garbage and the words are all pointers into .text/.rodata, so this is a data table, not a function. The old name already said 'embedded vtable block'; the new fact is that the xref callers (Model_DeletingDtor, Ui_MessageWindow_DtorDeleting, ...) cannot be real calls to a data address.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ClearChildState

The body contains no recipe data, so the first pass's 'RecipeBookState' wording was wrong and 'LayoutState' is the honest class.

summary: Tiny accessor: calls 0x001CF7F8 and returns the result minus 8, i.e. the base of an embedded instance header. 0x001CF7F8 is still unnamed, so the -8 could be a base or a container offset.

The callees recorded for the fragment (0x00490994, 0x0048FA08, 0x00497520) are the battle damage/agility math of the 0x0048xxxx range, which fits the BattleAi parent and contradicts the old 'Ui_TextLayout' prefix.

The sibling Ui_TextLayout_LayoutMode0 (0x00276428) is called on the same object, so the class is the text layout, not a status-message layout.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_InvokeVirtual138
summary: Thunk that calls the object's virtual slot +0x138 and returns 0; called from maybe_Actor_HasSpecialModelPart and maybe_Actor_QueryInteraction, so the receiver is an actor-side object, not a UI object.

name: Container_KeyedListEntry_DtorDelete

The 'refresh' half is supported; the 'TextSpan' class is not - nothing in the body mentions text.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectSprite_BindHandles
summary: Resolves a handle pair for a field sprite from its object record and stores it at sprite+0x10/+0x14, retrying with the record's secondary handle; on success it clears the owner's shared state word and dispatches to one of two interface objects of a global service singleton, selected by the kind byte in the resolved descriptor.
evidence: The body is readable and the retry/dispatch shape is verified, but every helper it uses (0x0065564C, 0x00655398, 0x00502BB8) is still unnamed and the recorded callee list (Fs_UnmountByName, Fs_FileRequest_Init, ...) does not match the body, so the xref range is unreliable.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_Reset
summary: Installs vtable 0x00768278 at self, releases the child at +8 through 0x0010F69C, clears +4, then resolves self+0x14 through 0x006F0934 and returns the result minus 0x14. The vtable store contradicts the old 'GetSceneNode' reading, which assumed a plain getter.
evidence: Disassembly 0x003A7AF8: `push {r4,r5,r6,lr}; ldr r0,[pc,#0x2c]; mov r5,#0; str r0,[r4]` - a vtable store, then `ldr r0,[r4,#8]; cmp r0,#0; beq ...` and the release call. A getter does not write a vtable, so the first-pass name was wrong; what the function is (constructor or destructor) is still open.
